Configure the OpenTelemetry pipeline so `claude_code.token.usage` events are pushed to a **readable local sink** (OTLP/file exporter). This is the hidden prerequisite that must exist before the token collector (next issue) can function.

## Purpose

Implement Project Model v1 advisory input support in Elenchus Core so it can review Build Arena's latest decomposition snapshots instead of treating them as unsupported.

Parent coordination issue: https://github.com/leonbreukelman/build-arena/issues/4

## Background

Build Arena now emits `project-model/v1` as the primary enriched decomposition artifact and `project-model/v0` only as a compatibility projection. Elenchus Core currently accepts/evaluates only `schemaVersion: project-model/v0`, so v1 snapshots cannot be reviewed directly.

Relevant Build Arena contract sources:

- `docs/schemas/project-model-v1.schema.json`
- `docs/specs/2026-06-05-project-model-v1-shared-contract-spec.md`
- `docs/verification/2026-06-05-pre-live-readiness-register.json`

Readiness item: `PMV1-002` remains open until Elenchus Core can consume v1.

## Implementation scope

Add v1 support alongside the existing v0 path. Do not remove or reinterpret v0.

- Add a `ProjectModelV1` parser/adapter or equivalent v1 ingestion path.

CI red on main: 1.85 (MSRV) job fails reproducibly — code passes locally, ARC runner logs not persisted

## Summary

`CI` has been **red on `main` for 6+ days** (since the last pushes on 2026-04-26). The failure is isolated to the **`1.85` (MSRV floor) matrix job**; `stable`, `beta`, and `wasm32 compilation check` all pass. I re-ran the failed job today (2026-06-06) — **it failed again**, so this is reproducible, not a flake.

| Job | Result |
|-----|--------|
| 1.85 | ❌ failure (reproduced on re-run) |
| stable | ✅ |
| beta | ✅ |
| wasm32 compilation check | ✅ |

Run: https://github.com/cachekit-io/cachekit-rs/actions/runs/26684715852

## The code is NOT the cause

The 1.85 job runs `cargo test --features "cachekitio,redis,encryption,l1,macros"`. I reproduced the **exact** command locally on `rustc 1.85.1` (same toolchain CI installs) — **everything is green**:

- `cargo +1.85 test --features "…"` → all suites `ok`, 0 failed
- `cargo +1.85 test --no-run --features "…"` → compiles clean
- `cargo +1.85 test --doc --features "…"` → doctests pass

Two per-agent onboarding concerns (Drawk, 2026-06-05) to build into Phase C, **before the ruby canary actually migrates**.

## 1. An agent's memory must follow it to the box
Each agent has accumulated **file-based memory** beyond its repo `CLAUDE.md` — its "things remembered." When it moves from the laptop to its permanent server home, that memory must come with it, or the agent arrives amnesiac.

### The load-bearing constraint: Claude Code memory is **path-keyed**
On the laptop an agent's memory lives at `~/.claude/projects/<project-slug>/memory/` (a `MEMORY.md` index + individual `*.md` files), where `<project-slug>` is the project's **absolute path with `/` → `-`**. Verified on disk:

- On the box ruby runs as `agent-ruby` from `/home/agent-ruby/repos/basecradle-ruby`, so its slug **changes** to `-home-agent-ruby-repos-basecradle-ruby`. **A naïve copy won't be found** — the migration must relocate the memory to the *server-side* slug.

title: Selection mode leaves blank space to the right and does not respond to window resize
text:
Selection mode leaves blank space to the right and does not respond to window resize

## Summary
In the directory selection view, the results pane stops at a fixed width and leaves a growing blank area on the right side. Resizing the window wider does not expand the track area, toolbar, or spectrum section to fill the available space.

## Reproduction
1. Open the comparison panel in directory selection mode (the screen that shows the file tree on the left and the preview/results pane on the right).
2. Make the window wide, or resize it wider after the view is visible.
3. Observe the right side of the track area.

## Actual
The right pane keeps roughly the same width, and empty space appears to the right of the tracks. Window resize does not cause the preview/results pane to stretch to the new width.

## Expected
The right-side results pane should flex to fill the remaining horizontal space inside the selection layout, and the track area should resize with the window.

## Evidence
I reproduced this in a standalone Chromium preview of the selection-mode ComparisonPanel. The selection body width changed with the viewport, but the results pane stayed fixed at 848 px:

- viewport 1600 px: body 1600 px, results pane 848 px, right gap 448 px
- viewport 1800 px: body 1800 px, results pane 848 px, right gap 648 px

## Suspected cause
The selection layout uses a horizontal flex container, but the results pane does not appear to participate in flex growth:

- src/webview/panels/ComparisonPanel.ts: `#selection-body { display: flex; }`
- src/webview/panels/ComparisonPanel.

Computing `num_patches_y` globally over the entire batch using `ops.max(pos_y_safe) + 1` is highly problematic when batching images of different aspect ratios. If one image in the batch is extremely tall (large `Y`) and another is extremely wide (large `X`), the global `num_patches_y` will scale up the `flat_pos` of the wide image quadratically, easily exceeding `mm_posemb_size` and causing out-of-bounds index errors or crashes. Computing `num_patches_y` per-image along the last axis resolves this issue completely.

```suggestion
        num_patches_y = ops.cast(
            ops.maximum(ops.max(pos_y_safe, axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1, 1), "int32"
        )
        flat_pos = pos_x_safe * num_patches_y + pos_y_safe

title: W3 — ticket lanes: per-team declared vocabulary over the task queue
text:
W3 — ticket lanes: per-team declared vocabulary over the task queue

## Design (settled with RJ, 2026-06-04)

Lanes are **data, not doctrine** — a per-team declared vocabulary over the existing task queue. No second store (workspace ticket files would recreate the drift problem #103 solved). Different teams = different recipes; nobody designs lanes at the framework level again.

### Declaration (team yaml / recipe passthrough)
```yaml
lanes: true        # shorthand → backlog → working → review → done
# or the full form:
lanes:
  - id: backlog
  - id: working
  - id: review
    description: The editor checks claims and tone; nothing leaves review without their pass.
    gate: seo_editor          # only this member (or a human) moves tasks OUT of this lane
  - id: done
```

### Mechanics (uniform, runtime-enforced)
- `lane:` label on tasks, validated against the team's declared list; every move audited (`task.lane_moved`)
- Verbs as CLI + capability actions: `task.take` (→ working), `task.complete` (→ next lane), `task.move` (explicit)
- **Both agents and humans move tickets** — except out of a gated lane, where only the `gate` member or a human may (the one place mechanics touch meaning, opt-in per lane)
- Teams without `lanes:` and solo agents: zero ceremony (pure opt-in, per the original W3 deferral)

### Meaning (prose, context-injected)
Each lane's `description` is injected into the team's context layer — agents behave per *their team's* definition of "review". Same pattern as SOUL.md: config declares, prose instructs, the runtime never har

Turn the existing Find Yours quiz into an intelligent guided discovery funnel with visible match percentages, explanation logic, recommended characters, and inquiry handoff.

title: install: aborted --with-driver leaves docker nvidia toggle off (no trap restore)
text:
install: aborted --with-driver leaves docker nvidia toggle off (no trap restore)

## Summary

`install-mig-sysext.sh --with-driver` disables the Apps NVIDIA toggle (`docker.update '{"nvidia": false}'`) as part of releasing the GPU before the driver swap, but — unlike `uninstall-mig-sysext.sh` and `recover-stock-nvidia.sh` — its abort trap does **not** re-enable it. An aborted install therefore leaves the toggle stuck `false` with no auto-restore.

This is not a regression from #55 (which intentionally scoped install's trap to the `/usr` readonly restore) — the toggle-disable was added to install by #59 (per-app GPU release), after #55 was written. The dangerous failure mode (`/usr` left writable) **is** covered by #55. This issue is only about the toggle.

## Detail

- Install disables the toggle at `scripts/install-mig-sysext.sh:1219` and `:1245`.
- Install's trap is `cleanup_tmp` (`scripts/install-mig-sysext.sh:1001`, `trap … EXIT INT TERM`), which restores `readonly=on` only — no toggle restore.
- By contrast, `uninstall-mig-sysext.sh` (`restore_state`, line ~71) and `recover-stock-nvidia.sh` (`restore_state`, line ~54) both re-enable the toggle in their trap **and** on the success path.

## Why it may be acceptable as-is

`--with-driver` install requires a reboot, and `configure-mig` (run after reboot) re-enables the toggle. So install deliberately leaves the toggle `false` even on the success path — apps are GPU-less until the post-reboot `configure-mig`. An aborted install lands in the same toggle state as a successful one, and is self-healing: re-ru

TranscriptMirror watches wrong project_dir when working_dir is relative or contains dots

## Bug

\`TranscriptMirrorCog\` ends up tailing a directory that never exists, so in \`CLORD_BRIDGE_MODE=jsonl\` **no Claude responses are ever posted to Discord**.

## Root causes (two separate bugs in \`derive_project_dir\`)

### 1. Relative \`working_dir\` is not resolved to absolute before slugifying

\`working_dir\` is stored in the DB as a relative path (\`data/sessions/<guild>/<thread>\`), relative to c-lord's CWD.
\`derive_project_dir\` passes it through \`cwd.replace("/", "-")\` unchanged, producing:

\`\`\`
~/.claude/projects/data-sessions-<guild>-<thread>   # wrong – does not exist
\`\`\`

Claude Code always records its CWD as an **absolute** path, so the actual project directory is:

\`\`\`
~/.claude/projects/-home-kaiono--config-c-lord-data-sessions-<guild>-<thread>  # correct
\`\`\`

### 2. Dots in path components are not replaced with \`-\`

Claude Code's slug algorithm replaces **both** \`/\` **and** \`.\` with \`-\`.
\`derive_project_dir\` only replaces \`/\`, so \`.config\` stays as \`.config\` instead of becoming \`-config\`, producing another slug mismatch.

For example, \`/home/kaiono/.config/c-lord/\` should slug to \`-home-kaiono--config-c-lord-\` but currently produces \`-home-kaiono-.config-c-lord-\`.

## Reproduction

1. Set \`CLORD_BRIDGE_MODE=jsonl\`.
2. Run c-lord from a directory where \`working_dir\` is stored as a relative path **or** the absolute path contains a dotted component (\`.config\`, \`.local\`, etc.).
3. Observe the \`TranscriptMirro

title: Add a rotated/correlated Gaussian analytical target to validate Powell's conjugate-direction update (and CMA-ES rotation)
text:
Add a rotated/correlated Gaussian analytical target to validate Powell's conjugate-direction update (and CMA-ES rotation)

## Summary

The analytical integration harness (`AnalyticalModel` / `tests/integration_harness.py`) only supports an **axis-aligned (diagonal-variance) Gaussian**. That is a *separable* objective: Powell (#403) solves it in a single cycle along the coordinate axes, so the `powell` mode-recovery test **never exercises the conjugate-direction (direction-replacement) machinery** — the core of Powell's method. CMA-ES's covariance adaptation is now exercised by the banana test, but a clean *unimodal* correlated test would complement it.

Add a **rotated / correlated Gaussian** analytical target (a full covariance matrix, i.e. a quadratic bowl with off-diagonal curvature) and use it to test the conjugate-direction path directly.

## Why

A rotated quadratic is the textbook validator for conjugate-direction methods: with coordinate directions alone, descent zig-zags and is slow; Powell's direction-set update builds mutually conjugate directions that converge in `n` cycles. Unlike the banana (#403 analysis), a quadratic is **unimodal with no line-search traps**, so the parabolic line search is exact and the test isolates the *direction update* rather than line-search robustness. It also gives CMA-ES a clean correlated-but-unimodal recovery test distinct from the banana.

## Scope

- Extend `AnalyticalModel` to evaluate `0.5 * (x-mu)^T Σ^{-1} (x-mu)` for a supplied covariance `Σ` (and a `rotated_gaussian` spec + `H.rotated_gaussian_spec(...)` helper); keep `ground_truth` (mode = `mu`)

title: Make polygon plots approximate while keeping summary stats exact
text:
Make polygon plots approximate while keeping summary stats exact

## Problem
Large polygon samples still take longer than expected because /stats/scatter does more work than the summary cards need. The endpoint currently reads polygon windows multiple times to compute exact 1D histograms and paired scatter/2D histograms, even though the plotted data is capped and can be approximate.

## Desired behavior
- Keep summary statistics exact: count, sum, average, valid area, and valid percent.
- Allow histogram/scatter outputs to be approximate/sample-based for performance.
- Avoid extra raster passes just to populate approximate plots.
- Keep plot payloads bounded so the histogram/scatter view is not cluttered.
- Preserve existing response shape where practical.

## Acceptance criteria
- Exact summary stats are computed from all valid pixels inside the polygon.
- 1D histograms are built from bounded sampled values rather than a second full raster pass.
- Paired scatter/2D histogram uses bounded sampled pairs rather than a full additional polygon scan where possible.
- Large polygons should do materially less raster IO than the current implementation.
- UI communicates that plots are sampled/approximate while summaries remain exact.

fix(estimate-builder): flush pending autosave on unmount (lost-edit-on-navigate)

## Parent

#458 — PRD: Flush pending autosave on unmount in the Estimate/Invoice builder.

## What to build

Wire the `planUnmountFlush` planner (from #460) into the `useAutoSave` hook so
that when the builder unmounts while dirty, the pending edits are **flushed**
instead of discarded. This is the slice that actually fixes the user-visible
lost-edit-on-navigate bug for Estimates and Invoices.

Add a **latest-ref** (reassigned every render so a mount-only cleanup reads fresh
state, exempt from exhaustive-deps) plus a mount-only unmount `useEffect` whose
cleanup calls the ref. On unmount it builds the plan from the current entity and
snapshot refs, then fires each `PlannedWrite` via
`fetch(path, { method: "PUT", keepalive: true, … })`, fire-and-forget. The
fetch loop stays a thin wrapper around the pure planner — no diff logic duplicated
here.

This mirrors the #443 photo-report `flushOnUnmountRef` pattern. The hook's public
return (`UseAutoSaveResult`) is unchanged; the fix is internal. All three builder
entry points (estimate, invoice, template) inherit it with no per-call wiring.

**In scope:** in-app navigation (component unmount) only.
**Out of scope:** hard tab-close / refresh (`pagehide` / `beforeunload`) — a known
gap deferred to a follow-up, along with its test (see PRD #458).

title: Worktree chains vanish on upgrade: 0.3.1 wrote worktree-local refs/zhi, 0.3.8 reads shared refs/zhi, no migration (silent empty, looks like data loss)
text:
Worktree chains vanish on upgrade: 0.3.1 wrote worktree-local refs/zhi, 0.3.8 reads shared refs/zhi, no migration (silent empty, looks like data loss)

## Summary

A chain created by an older git-zhi inside a **linked worktree** becomes invisible after upgrading the binary — `git zhi list` / `milestone list` read it as empty — because the two versions store `refs/zhi/` in **different ref namespaces**. No data is lost, but it silently looks like total data loss.

## What happened (concrete)

1. With `v0.3.1-40-gb22c491`, inside a linked worktree, created milestone `codegen-harness` + 12 issues. `git zhi list` showed all 12. ✅
2. Upgraded the binary to `v0.3.8`.
3. `git zhi list` now shows **empty**; `git zhi milestone list` shows only the shared `v0.1` (and a new 0.3.8-created milestone), NOT `codegen-harness`.
4. The data is intact: the **old 0.3.1 binary still lists all 12 issues** from the same worktree. And on disk:

```
# 0.3.1 wrote the chain to the WORKTREE-LOCAL ref dir:
.git/worktrees/pu/refs/zhi/_/issues/019e9a26-f0aa-...   (12 issues)
.git/worktrees/pu/refs/zhi/_/milestones/codegen-harness  (implied)

# 0.3.8 reads/writes the SHARED (common-dir) ref dir:
.git/refs/zhi/_/milestones/v0.1
.git/refs/zhi/_/milestones/zhi68-smoketest   (created by 0.3.8)
```

So 0.3.1 stored worktree chains under the worktree-local `refs/zhi/` (`.git/worktrees/<name>/refs/zhi/`), while 0.3.8 uses the shared common-dir `refs/zhi/`. After upgrade, 0.3.8 doesn't look in the worktree-local namespace, so the chain "disappears."

title: Stats dashboard counts multi-day sessions only on their start date (Active days / streaks / peak hour undercounted)
text:
Stats dashboard counts multi-day sessions only on their start date (Active days / streaks / peak hour undercounted)

## Summary

The desktop client's **Stats** dashboard (Overview tab 鈥?*Active days*, *Current/Longest streak*, *Peak hour*, and the activity heatmap) buckets each entire session under the date/hour of its **first message only**. Any session that spans multiple calendar days (a long-running or resumed/forked conversation) is counted as activity on its **start day alone**; every subsequent day silently disappears from these metrics.

## Environment

- Claude desktop (Windows, MSIX): `Claude_1.11187.1.0_x64`
- Bundled Claude Code CLI: `2.1.161`
- OS: Windows 11, local timezone UTC+8

## Symptoms (real example)

On a machine with **7 sessions / 5,570 messages** whose transcript activity actually spans **8 consecutive local days (2026-05-30 鈫?2026-06-06)**:

| Metric | Shown | Correct |
|---|---|---|
| Active days | **2** | 8 |
| Longest streak | **1d** | 8d |
| Current streak | **0d** | 8d |
| Peak hour | hour sessions were *started* | should reflect when messages actually occurred |
| Heatmap | only 2 cells lit | 8 cells |

Cross-check: `Total tokens`, `Messages`, `Sessions`, and `Favorite model` are **correct**, because those are accumulated per-message. Only the **day/hour-bucketed** metrics are wrong.

## Root cause

In the stats aggregation routine, each transcript file's day/hour bucket is derived from the **first** message's timestamp, and the whole session is attributed to that single bucket:

title: Vessel targets are bound by bare slice index — every slate mutation can mistarget the wrong vessel
text:
Vessel targets are bound by bare slice index — every slate mutation can mistarget the wrong vessel

Root cause (#9): `spacecraft/target.go` stores a raw `CraftIdx` into `World.Crafts` with **no stable vessel identity/generation**. Every operation that mutates the craft slate (end-flight removal, dock, undock) shifts indices but does **not** remap stored `Target.CraftIdx`, so surviving craft-targets silently re-point at a *different* vessel (off-by-one, past the existing bounds checks). This is one design fix, not many patches — give vessels a stable ID and resolve targets by identity, or funnel every slate mutation through a single index-remap helper. **ADR-worthy.** Contains a HIGH-severity case (#2).

---

### 🔴 `internal/sim/end_flight.go:45` — HIGH (CONFIRMED)

**EndFlightActive removes a craft from the slate but never remaps Target.CraftIdx, so any craft-target pointing past the removed slot silently mistargets the wrong (or aliased) vessel.**

*Failure:* Slate [A(0,crashed,active), B(1), C(2)]; player has B targeting C (B.Target = {TargetCraft, CraftIdx:2}). Press [E] on A: w.Crafts becomes [B(0), C(1)], then SetActiveCraftIdx(0) reloads w.Target from B's stored Target with CraftIdx:2 — now out of range (silently dropped) when it should be C at index 1; in the symmetric case where a craft targeted index 1 and a lower craft is removed, CraftIdx:2 now resolves to a different vessel. The bounds checks in target.go/rendezvous.go only catch out-of-range, not the off-by-one mistarget.

Cleanup: doc-comment drift & dead code in the core

Low-priority cleanup. Doc comments that contradict the code (#35 NaN node-angle sentinel, #37 porkchop param label, #41 inverted prograde comment), a dead `finiteburn` guard (#38), a dead `PredictedSegments` wrapper that nil-derefs (#42), and a duplicated `Stages` copy in save (#36).

---

### 🟢 `internal/orbital/kepler.go:227` — LOW (CONFIRMED)

**The Readout doc contract states node angle fields are NaN for equatorial/circular orbits, but OrbitReadout actually emits el.Omega (0) for AscNode and Omega+pi (pi) for DescNode, so the documented NaN sentinel never appears.**

*Failure:* A caller that trusts the documented contract and uses math.IsNaN(ro.AscNode) to decide whether to render '—' would always see a finite value and print a meaningless '0.0 deg / 180.0 deg' node for an equatorial orbit. Current in-repo consumers dodge this by guarding on Inclination < tol instead, so the defect is a doc/contract inaccuracy rather than a live wrong-render; any future caller following the comment is misled.

Line 64: "circular orbits (Ω and ω then undefined — left at zero rather than NaN)."

Lines 112-125: ElementsFromState initializes `var omega float64` (= 0) and only sets it when `nMag > 0`; for equatorial orbits nMag == 0, so omega stays 0.

Lines 225-227 (Readout doc): "for equatorial / circular orbits the corresponding fields are NaN (callers render '—' or skip)."

title: Cache configuration TTL accepts zero or negative values, causing immediate expiration or infinite validity

Cache configuration TTL accepts zero or negative values, causing immediate expiration or infinite validity

Latest comment:
Hi @agnivo988,

Contributed as part of GSSoC '26. I have addressed Issue #445 by implementing strict time-to-live (TTL) validation mechanisms for our cache configuration layers.

### What was fixed:
- **Boundary Validation:** Enforced defensive constraints within `internal/cache/cache.go`, clamping down acceptable TTL allocations strictly between 1 minute and 7 days.
- **Regression Engineering:** Added an extensive table-driven testing block inside `internal/cache/cache_test.go` confirming that invalid profiles (negative intervals, instantaneous zeroes, or overflow durations) are intercepted correctly.

### Why it was necessary:
- Unchecked values permitted runtime instability, causing memory leaks through infinite retention or cache thrashing due to instantaneous expirations.

title: [API] App settings: migration, service, endpoints, and integrations UI
text:
[API] App settings: migration, service, endpoints, and integrations UI

### Overview

Single persistent store for all integration credentials. Every future integration (USDA, OFF, Mealie) reads its key from here — no env var juggling for the user.

### Deliverable 1 — Migration 010

New table `app_settings`: `key` (TEXT primary key), `value` (TEXT nullable), `updated_at` (timestamp). No UUID — `key` is the identity. Seed all known keys with `value=null` so `GET /api/settings` always returns a complete list without code needing a hardcoded fallback. Known keys seeded: `usda_api_key`, `off_username`, `off_password`, `mealie_url`, `mealie_api_key`.

### Deliverable 2 — `AppSetting` SQLModel class

`server/src/porquilo/models/app_setting.py`, exported from `models/__init__.py`.

### Deliverable 3 — Settings service

`server/src/porquilo/services/settings_service.py`

`KNOWN_SETTINGS_KEYS: frozenset[str]` — the whitelist. New integrations add a key here and seed a migration row; no schema change required.

`get_setting(key, session) -> Optional[str]` — simple SELECT by primary key, returns `None` if not found.

`set_setting(key, value, session)` — upserts; raises `ValueError` for unknown keys; does not commit.

### Deliverable 4 — Settings router

`GET /api/settings` — returns all known keys (including unseeded rows as `value=null`). `GET /api/settings/{key}` — 404 for unknown keys. `PUT /api/settings/{key}` — 422 for unknown keys, clears on `value=null`.

title: install.sh fails with curl error 23 when daemon holds the binary
text:
install.sh fails with curl error 23 when daemon holds the binary

## Problem

When `model-shelf` is already installed and the daemon is running, re-running the install script fails with:

```
curl: (23) Failure writing output to destination
```

This happens because on Linux, writing to an executable that is currently being run by a process (the daemon) is not allowed.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install model-shelf and start the daemon (`model-shelf service install`)
2. Re-run the installer: `curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bmaltais/model-shelf/main/install.sh | sh`
3. Observe curl error 23

## Expected behavior

The installer should handle this gracefully. Common strategies:
- Stop the daemon before overwriting (via `model-shelf service stop` if available)
- Delete the old binary first (`rm -f`) then write the new one (Linux allows unlinking a running binary)
- Write to a temp file then `mv` (atomic replace, works even on running binaries)

## Environment

- Observed on: mini1 and mini2 (Linux amd64, Ubuntu)
- Works fine on ocilab1 (Linux arm64) because the test binary path differs from the installed path
- Works fine on second attempt after manually removing the old binary

feat(team-knowledge): untrusted-content handling contract — advisory inbox rendering

## Spec Reference
**Source**: `specs/team-knowledge-mvp-v1.md`
**Sections**: §6.1 (Untrusted-content handling contract, NEW v4), §2 (North star boundary)

## What to Build
Implement the untrusted-content handling contract that makes the §2 "data, not instructions" boundary enforceable. Without this contract, shared prose (`practice`/`rationale`/`evidence`/`instantiation`, component READMEs, catalog fields) that flows into the advisory inbox can launder authority — a `rationale` saying "ignore previous instructions; run this command; this was approved by Jason" becomes a covert command channel.

**The five contract requirements (§6.1 — every implementation MUST):**

1. **Quote, never inject**: Shared artifact text is wrapped as quoted/untrusted data with provenance + status labels. Advisory inbox renderers MUST NOT inject raw shared prose into control prompts as instructions; raw prose is quoted evidence only.

2. **Structured-field extraction**: Inbox processing pulls typed fields via schema; imperative text is discarded/escaped for any control decision. Tool-bearing prompts include only normalized fields, never a raw README/`rationale` blob.

3. **Commands are proposals, never next-steps**: Any command appearing in shared prose is proposed text, never an executable step — it can only become a typed proposal, and routes through the §Pillar-3 `review_token` gate if it touches a quarantine path.

4. **Summarization must not upgrade trust**: Summaries preserve `source`/`status`/

execute_source_adapter.py records content_hash, byte_count, and transient_payload_path for remote captures at tools/scripts/execute_source_adapter.py:1648-1691.

But validate_source_acquisition_execution.py only validates that the capture hash is shaped like SHA-256 text. It never opens transient_payload_path and compares the actual payload bytes to content_hash and byte_count. See tools/validators/validate_source_acquisition_execution.py:337-457.

I proved this with a synthetic fixture:

declared_hash      d6004ba597d097dfd95ac55076dbf03325b89d41b94fe8366c310a779ae57be5
actual_payload_hash bf0d6d3f14b00453cb97ecac5518862b111129bdad240982948257fb1cc6100c

errors []

That means a remote payload can be corrupted, swapped, or deleted after JSONL generation and still pass validation.

PRD: In-app document viewer with a slim page picker for Estimate & Invoice views

> Originates from #457 ("Estimate viewer UI fix."). This is the **parent PRD**; implementation slices will be cut from it via `/to-issues`.

## Problem Statement

When I open an **Estimate** (or **Invoice**) to *view* it, the strip of page thumbnails — the **page picker** — eats roughly **half** the width of the viewer. The document I actually want to read is squeezed into the other half. On a normal-width screen the picker only needs to be about **a quarter** of the width, with the document getting the rest. Today I have no way to make that happen: the picker, the toolbar, and the zoom controls are all the **browser's built-in PDF viewer**, which we embed in a bare `<iframe>`. Its sidebar width is browser chrome — it cannot be styled, resized, or constrained from our application. So "make the page picker a quarter" is literally impossible while we delegate viewing to the browser.

## Solution

Stop delegating the View surface to the browser's native PDF chrome. Render the customer-facing **Estimate** / **Invoice** PDF in an **in-app document viewer** we fully control, built on the `react-pdf` / pdf.js stack the contracts flow already uses. The viewer is a two-pane layout:

- A **slim page picker rail** on the left — about **a quarter** of the width, collapsible, and hidden on narrow/mobile screens.
- The **document pane** filling the remaining width, showing all pages in a continuous vertical scroll.

But execute_local_git_repo() then reads files from the working tree with file_path.read_bytes() at tools/scripts/execute_source_adapter.py:1148-1151.

This PR fixes LibreMesh mesh networking (babeld) in the QEMU testbed by letting `lime-config` run normally, then overriding only the network layer via a new `rc.local` (DHCP on `br-lan`, plain babeld restart), disabling bridge multicast snooping so babeld hellos are flooded to all TAP ports, and adding a `lime-proto-babeld` defconfig entry so `lime-config` actually wires babeld rather than silently falling back to bmx7. - **`configure-source-image.sh`** – New `rc.local` atomically rewrites `/etc/config/network` and `/etc/config/babeld` post lime-config, waits up to 30 s for `br-lan` UP, then starts babeld via its init script; the first-boot marker is only written when both conditions are verified, making a failed boot automatically retry. - **`configure-vms.sh`*

## Spec Reference
**Source**: `specs/team-knowledge-mvp-v1.md`
**Sections**: §Pillar 3 (steps 4-5), §6 (v1 controls), §9 item 5

## What to Build
Implement the ComponentReview intake gate (Pillar 3 step 4) and the mechanical `review_token` adapt-gate (step 5). Both are required from day one — step 5 is NOT optional; without it, the F2 hole (adapt-phase silently executes) is re-introduced.

**Gate 4 — ComponentReview intake (agent-b):**
- Quarantine-clone the **pinned SHA** into an isolated path outside any agent-trusted directory (never into `.claude/`, hooks, skills, or any exec/trust path)

title: PR review on coolabnet/libremesh-lab
text: PR review on coolabnet/libremesh-lab Review comment: **`--debug` is parsed but still forwarded to `main "$@"`** The `for arg in "$@"` loop recognises `--debug` and sets `DEBUG=1`, but the original `$@` is never modified, so `main "$@"` receives `--debug` as a positional argument. `main` does not parse positional arguments today, so it is silently ignored — but any future change that makes `main` iterate `"$@"` (e.g. to accept a node filter) would receive an unexpected `--debug` string. Standard practice is to rebuild the positional list after parsing, e.g. with a `set --` call or a separate `MAIN_ARGS` array that omits recognised flags.

title: status command only shows local jobs — no aggregated view across mesh
text:
status command only shows local jobs — no aggregated view across mesh

## Problem

`model-shelf status` (without a job ID) only shows jobs that were executed on the local node. There is no way to see all jobs across the mesh from a single node.

## Current behavior

```bash
# On ocilab1 — only shows jobs executed locally
model-shelf status
# Shows: 3 jobs (all target=ocilab1)

# On mini1 — shows different jobs
ssh mini1 'model-shelf status'
# Shows: 2 jobs (target=mini1 and target=mini2 dispatched from ocilab1)
```

## Expected behavior

title: 宣言から削除されたリソースの実体とステータスが残ることがある
text:
宣言から削除されたリソースの実体とステータスが残ることがある

## 概要

実機検証中に、`router.yaml` から `TailscaleNode/homert03` を削除して `routerd` を再起動しても、過去に生成された systemd unit や routerd のトップレベル `Error` 状態が残る挙動を確認した。

## 観測した挙動

- `hosts/homert03/router.yaml` から `TailscaleNode/homert03` を削除した
- `routerd validate` は成功した
- `routerd.service` を再起動しても、以前生成された `routerd-tailscale-homert03.service` が残っていた
- 手動で以下を実行するまで実体が残った
  - `systemctl disable --now routerd-tailscale-homert03.service`
  - `/etc/systemd/system/routerd-tailscale-homert03.service` の削除
  - `systemctl reset-failed routerd-tailscale-homert03.service`
  - `systemctl daemon-reload`
- その後も `routerctl get --list-kinds` には `TailscaleNode` が出なくなった一方で、`routerctl status` のトップレベル `phase` は `Error` のまま残った
- 個別 controller には `currentError: false` しか見えず、どの削除済みリソースがトップレベル `Error` を引き上げているのか分かりにくい

## 期待する挙動

宣言から削除された管理対象リソースについて、routerd が以下を行う。

- 生成済みの外部実体を停止・削除する
- systemd unit であれば disable/stop、unit ファイル削除、daemon-reload、failed state の整理まで行う
- routerd 内部のリソースステータスやトップレベル phase から削除済みリソース由来の stale error を消す
- 削除対象が cleanup できない場合は、残っている対象と理由を `routerctl status` / `describe` から追跡できるようにする

## 再現環境

- routerd: `v20260528.2308 (575de94f)`
- 対象: homert03 / Ubuntu 24.04 LTS
- リソース: `TailscaleNode/homert03`

## 関連

HA 構成テスト中に見つかった。`when` が偽になった時の停止・削除とは別に、宣言そのものから消えたリソースの garbage collection と stale status cleanup として扱うのがよさそう。

**Source**: `specs/team-knowledge-mvp-v1.md`

Implement `scripts/map_patterns.py` — the assembler that builds `CELL[area][dev]`, classifies each area row, and enforces the §1.6 adopted-pattern lifecycle state machine. This is the TARGET stage of SENSE→TARGET→INVEST: it points at where a shared pattern would pay off, but does not decide.

**MAP mechanic (§1.4) — two scopes:**

**Within-developer:** for each dev, does this dev apply the same `pattern_key` consistently across their own projects in an area, or diverge from themselves?

| Outcome | Condition |
|---|---|
| CONSENSUS | quorum (3/4) share a `pattern_key`; `occurrence_confidence >= 0.4`; `source` includes `observed` |

| GAP | key missing for some/all devs in a relevant area |

**UNMAPPED surfacing:** UNMAPPED entries are surfaced as taxonomy-gap signals in the map output — never force-bucketed, and counted toward GAP when they represent missing coverage.

title: epic(remote): publish MCP over the web with auth (single-tenant, Supabase Auth)
text:
epic(remote): publish MCP over the web with auth (single-tenant, Supabase Auth)

## ゴール

ローカル stdio 専用だった MCP サーバーを **Web 上にリモート公開**し、**Claude (Claude.ai / Desktop / Code)** から
リモートコネクタ経由で接続できるようにする。**シングルテナント（帳簿は1冊・利用者は自分だけ）を維持**したまま、
公開に必須となる**認証 (OAuth)** を導入する。

## 設計判断（確定事項）

- **マルチテナントは導入しない。** 帳簿は `AI_BOOKS_DB_URL` 1本のまま。`tenant_id` / RLS / ユーザー⇔帳簿の
  動的ルーティングは**不要**（AGENTS.md invariant #3「single-user 不変」を維持）。
- ただし **public 公開＝認証は必須**。stdio で OS のプロセス境界が担っていた認証が消えるため、
  「single-user でも門番は要る」。**認証 ≠ マルチテナント**。
- **IdP は Supabase Auth** を採用。理由: 既に Supabase を使用済み / FastMCP に `supabase` auth provider 同梱
  (`fastmcp.server.auth.providers.supabase`, FastMCP 3.3.1) / viewer (Next.js) と同一 IdP を共有できる。
- **認可は allowlist** で自分1人のみ通す（認証済みでも許可 subject/email 以外は拒否）。
- 既存 invariant #2「全書込はサーバー側検証を通る」は維持 → 公開しても不正仕訳が直接 DB に入らない。
- stdio 経路は**デフォルトとして温存**（feature flag で HTTP を opt-in）。既存のローカル/CI/テスト/invariant を壊さない。

## Wave 構成 / 子 issue

### Wave 0 — 前提整備（直列・後続のブロッカー）

- [ ] #108 feat(web): viewer auth gate via Supabase Auth (Next.js middleware, single user)

### Wave 2 — 統合・デプロイ

- [ ] #110 test(auth): reject unauthenticated/forbidden + assert stdio path intact

title: [High] Run-level normalization applied once per streamer causes double-normalization
text:
[High] Run-level normalization applied once per streamer causes double-normalization

one-line summary
`GRunAction::publish_run_data` calls `normalize_run_data` inside the streamer loop, so with >=2 run streamers the in-place-mutated run data gets divided by `events_processed` once per streamer.

**Affected files**: `gemc/actions/run/gRunAction.cc:283-293` (loop + call at :290), `gemc/actions/run/gRunAction.cc:297-348` (`normalize_run_data` mutates in place)

**Details**: `normalize_run_data` mutates the shared `run_data_collaction` in place — for each normalized variable it replaces the stored value with `value / norm` via `digitized->includeVariable(...)`:

```cpp
digitized->includeVariable(varName, static_cast<double>(intIt->second) / norm);
...
digitized->includeVariable(varName, dblIt->second / norm);
```

`publish_run_data` invokes it once per streamer, inside the loop:

```cpp
for (const auto &[name, gstreamer]: *gstreamer_run_map) {
    if (gstreamer == nullptr) { ... }

    normalize_run_data(run_data_collaction);   // <-- mutates the SAME collection every iteration

    gstreamer->publishRunData(run_data_collaction);
}
```

Because the mutation is persistent on the shared collection, the first streamer publishes `value/N`, the second publishes `value/N^2`, the third `value/N^3`, etc.

**Impact**: Any run with two or more run-mode streamers configured (e.g. a `root` and a `csv` run output) produces wrong normalized run-level observables in every streamer after the first. With a single run streamer the bug is latent.

**Proposed fix**: Normalize exactl

/* src/app/globals.css — bloco .dark (linha 195+) */

Tier 1 Claude Code hooks (fast feedback, not enforcement)

## User story
As the maintainer, I need in-loop Claude Code hooks that keep an honest agent on track, documented as non-authoritative fast feedback (not a security boundary).

## Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then)
- Given a new session, When it starts, Then the constitution's key rules are injected.

- Given a destructive command, When the user-scope deny hook runs, Then it blocks the command.

Adversarial Claude PR reviewer (required check, model-tiered)

## User story
As the maintainer, I need an **adversarial Claude agent** to review every PR against the constitution and the deterministic results, blocking merge when it finds problems, so quality is independently gated — without me approving and without a separate bot account.

## Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then)
- Given a PR whose deterministic checks are green, When the reviewer job runs, Then an adversarial Claude agent reviews the diff against the constitution + CI/SAST outputs in fresh context, and the `agent-review` check **fails (red)** if it finds violations, passing only if the change holds up.
- Given a PR touching gate-config paths, When it runs, Then the review uses the **Opus** tier; routine PRs may use **Sonnet** (never Haiku).
- Given branch protection, Then `agent-review` is a required status check, so a failing review blocks merge — no human or bot approval involved.

## Implementation plan (adversarial Claude as a required CHECK, not an approval)
1. No bot account, no PAT, no PR "approval." The gate is a required **status check** — a workflow job's own conclusion is a check run that branch protection can require. The default `GITHUB_TOKEN` can post check runs (it only can't *approve* PRs, which we don't use).
2. `.github/workflows/agent-review.yml`: **no top-level workflow `name:`**; job name `agent-review`; `permissions: {contents: read, pull-requests: read, checks: write}`.

title: Model explicit Codex auth modes in harness setup state
text:
Model explicit Codex auth modes in harness setup state

## Parent

- #12289

## What to build

Teach Warp to model Codex authentication as an explicit harness setup choice rather than assuming Codex always uses an OpenAI-compatible managed secret.

This slice should add a user-facing and internally persisted auth mode for Codex with at least two modes:

- `api_key`
- `native_codex_login`

A completed slice means the Codex setup/config state can represent which auth path the user selected, that selection survives the normal setup flow, and downstream Codex setup logic can branch on that mode instead of inferring behavior from the presence of `OPENAI_API_KEY` alone.

This slice does not need to complete native login itself yet. It only needs to make auth mode an explicit part of Codex harness configuration and readiness modeling.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Codex harness setup state can represent both `api_key` and `native_codex_login` as explicit auth modes.
- [ ] The selected Codex auth mode persists through the existing setup/config flow used to launch Codex-backed work.
- [ ] Downstream Codex setup logic can branch on the selected auth mode without inferring auth behavior indirectly from environment variables alone.

None - can start immediately.

title: 知识来自连接：从信息到洞察的认知跃迁
text:
知识来自连接：从信息到洞察的认知跃迁

# 知识来自连接

一个常见误区是：

信息越多，知识越多。

实际上：

信息 ≠ 知识。

知识产生于连接。

## 信息是点

阅读、文章、划线、新闻、博客，本质上都是信息点。

很多人不断收集信息。

最终拥有成千上万个知识点。

但这些点彼此孤立。

因此并没有形成真正的知识体系。

## 知识是线

当多个信息点被连接起来时。

知识开始产生。

例如：

- Prompt Injection
- Tool Injection
- Memory Poisoning

表面是三种攻击。

本质都在影响Agent行为。

于是形成：

Agent Manipulation。

知识第一次出现。

## 洞察是网络

进一步连接不同领域。

例如：

- Agent Security
- 权限管理
- 身份认证
- RBAC

会发现不同领域在解决相似问题。

此时形成洞察。

洞察本质上是在看似无关的事物之间发现共同规律。

## 为什么读书越多的人差距越大

很多人：

读100本书 = 100本书。

少数人：

读100本书 → 建立连接 → 形成自己的观点体系。

差距不在阅读量。

而在连接能力。

## 为什么Issue比笔记更有价值

笔记倾向于存储。

Issue倾向于提问。

提问天然要求建立连接。

例如：

Prompt Injection与传统XSS有什么共同点？

Agent与科举制度有什么共同规律？

Skill与人才培养体系有什么对应关系？

这些问题都会推动新的连接产生。

## 大脑本质上是连接机器

记忆不是存储事实。

而是存储关系。

连接越多。

理解越深。

记忆越牢固。

## AI时代最稀缺的能力

过去的问题是信息不足。

未来的问题是信息过剩。

当所有人都拥有相似的信息获取能力后。

真正拉开差距的将是连接能力。

即：

发现不同领域共同规律的能力。

## 一个认知模型

信息
→ 连接
→ 知识
→ 洞察
→ 决策
→ 能力

其中最稀缺的一步不是信息。

而是连接。

信息越来越便宜。

连接越来越昂贵。

阅读不会自动产生知识。

收藏不会自动产生知识。

知识产生于连接。

Imported from `/home/joe/projects/Summa/bugz` as batch-3 finding 4.

Bug: sqlite_safety.run_check() only runs PRAGMA integrity_check or PRAGMA quick_check:

tools/source_db_tools/sqlite_safety.py:38-50

Fix: backup/restore/profile checks should run both:

Fail the backup if either returns violations.

unspecified: apply_migrations() can commit unrelated caller work before migration

Imported from `/home/joe/projects/Summa/bugz` as batch-3 finding 5.

Severity: unspecified

Bug: apply_migrations() builds a script and runs conn.executescript(script):

tools/source_db_tools/canonical_store.py:663-683

script_parts = ["PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON;", "BEGIN IMMEDIATE;"]
...
script_parts.append("COMMIT;")
...
conn.executescript(script)

Python documents that executescript() implicitly commits any pending transaction before executing the SQL script.

Impact: if a caller has pending writes on the same connection and then calls apply_migrations(), those writes can be committed outside the caller’s intended rollback boundary.

Fix: refuse to run if conn.in_transaction is true, or use a fresh migration-only connection.

title: make start fails with 'invalid hostPort' due to inline comment in .env
text:
make start fails with 'invalid hostPort' due to inline comment in .env

### Summary
`make start` aborts immediately with:

```
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml up -d --remove-orphans
invalid hostPort: 5434
make: *** [start] Error 1
```

### Root cause
The Makefile loads the env file with `-include .env` followed by `export`. When a
line in `.env` has an **inline comment**, GNU Make strips the `#…` comment but keeps
the trailing whitespace between the value and the comment. So a line like:

```
POSTGRES_PORT=5434                                # host port; avoids conflicts...
```

is exported as `POSTGRES_PORT="5434                   "` (value + trailing spaces).
Docker Compose substitutes that into the port mapping `"${POSTGRES_PORT:-5432}:5432"`,
producing a host port full of whitespace, which the port parser rejects →
`invalid hostPort: 5434`.

(Compose's own `.env` parser handles inline comments fine — the breakage comes from
Make re-exporting the same file as the source of truth for both.)

### Fix
Put comments on their own line so values have no trailing whitespace:

```
# host port; avoids conflicts with other PostgreSQL instances
POSTGRES_PORT=5434
```

### Suggested hardening
Any of these would prevent recurrence:
- Audit `.env` / `.env.example` for other inline-commented values that Make exports.
- Strip trailing whitespace from values in the Makefile, or stop sourcing `.env` into
  Make and rely on Compose's parser alone.
- Validate critical port vars before `docker compose up`.

### Environment
- Host: macOS (arm64 / Apple Silicon)

title: [Medium] gemc-sqlite CLI builds queries via raw f-strings (breakage + SQL injection)
text:
[Medium] gemc-sqlite CLI builds queries via raw f-strings (breakage + SQL injection)

The `gemc-sqlite` CLI assembles WHERE clauses and the SELECT column list with raw f-string interpolation of user-supplied values. Any value containing a quote breaks the query, and the values are a SQL injection vector.

**Affected files**

- `subprojects/pygemc/src/pygemc/api/gsqlite.py:61-91` (`main`, filter construction)
- `subprojects/pygemc/src/pygemc/api/gsqlite.py:124-141` (`show_volumes_from_database`, `show_materials_from_database`)

**Details**

```python
if args.ef:
	experiment_filter = f" WHERE experiment = '{args.ef}'"
...
if args.rf:
	...
	runno_filter = f' WHERE run = {args.rf}'

all_filters = experiment_filter + variation_filter + system_filter + runno_filter
...
show_volumes_from_database(sqlitedb, what, all_filters)
```

and:

```python
def show_volumes_from_database(sqlitedb, what, all_filters):
	...
	query = "SELECT {} FROM geometry {};".format(what, all_filters)
	sql.execute(query)
```

The filter values (`args.ef`, `args.vf`, `args.sf`, `args.rf`) and the column list (`args.what`) are interpolated directly into the SQL text. A value like `O'Brien` breaks the query; a value like `' OR '1'='1` (or worse, a stacked statement on a writable connection) is an injection. `what` and the table name cannot be bound as parameters, but should be validated against an allowlist of known columns.

**Impact**

CLI breaks on any value containing a single quote, and accepts arbitrary SQL through the filter and `-what` flags. Even on a read-mostly tool this is a real injec

title: [Low] convert_angle(out='gon') returns radians instead of gradians
text:
[Low] convert_angle(out='gon') returns radians instead of gradians

`convert_angle` accepts `'gon'` as a valid output unit (it is a key in `ANG_TO_RAD`) but only special-cases `deg`/`degree` on the return path. For `out='gon'` it falls through and returns the value in radians, not gradians.

**Affected files**

- `subprojects/pygemc/src/pygemc/api/g4_units.py:12-14` (`ANG_TO_RAD`)
- `subprojects/pygemc/src/pygemc/api/g4_units.py:186-193` (`convert_angle`)

**Details**

```python
ANG_TO_RAD = {
    'rad': 1.0, 'deg': math.pi / 180.0, 'degree': math.pi / 180.0, 'gon': math.pi / 200.0
}
...
def convert_angle(expr: str, out: str = 'deg') -> float:
    if out not in ANG_TO_RAD and out not in ('deg', 'degree', 'rad'):
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown output angle unit: {out}")
    names = {**ANG_TO_RAD}
    val_rad = _safe_eval(expr, names)
    if out in ('deg', 'degree'):
        return val_rad * (180.0 / math.pi)
    return val_rad
```

`out='gon'` passes the validation guard but is not handled in the return logic, so the function returns `val_rad` (radians) unchanged. Callers requesting gradians silently get radians.

**Impact**

Low severity (gon is rarely used), but a silent wrong-unit result for a documented-as-valid output. The asymmetric handling (only deg/degree converted) is the root cause.

**Proposed fix**

Convert generally using the `ANG_TO_RAD` table for any output unit rather than special-casing degrees. `val_rad / ANG_TO_RAD[out]` gives the value in the requested unit (and reduces to the existing deg/rad behavior).

Session-cleanup detector flags gate-events.jsonl (L0 token fallback log) as untagged tracking file → cleanup deletes live audit trail

## Summary

The session-cleanup detector flags `.copilot-tracking/gate-events.jsonl` as an "untagged tracking file" eligible for cleanup, and emits a `post-merge-cleanup.ps1 -UntaggedTrackingFiles @('.copilot-tracking/gate-events.jsonl')` command. But `gate-events.jsonl` is the **documented global fallback log for L0 gate-decision tokens** (`skills/solution-authoring/SKILL.md` § "L0 Gate Token", line ~244: *"Fallback: `.copilot-tracking/gate-events.jsonl` when session memory is unavailable."*). Running the suggested cleanup deletes live gate-audit history that the L2 reconciliation validator and L3 Code-Critic rely on to detect never-surfaced engagement-gate skips.

## Evidence

Observed this session — the `SessionStart` hook injected:

> **Post-merge cleanup detected** — stale tracking artifacts found:
> - 1 tracking file(s) with no issue ID found in `.copilot-tracking/`:
>   - `.copilot-tracking/gate-events.jsonl`
> ```
> pwsh '.../post-merge-cleanup.ps1' -UntaggedTrackingFiles @('.copilot-tracking/gate-events.jsonl')
> ```

The file currently holds 37+ live gate-decision/structured-question event entries.

## Root cause

`skills/session-startup/scripts/session-cleanup-detector-core.ps1:806`

```powershell
$persistentTrackingSubtrees = @(
    'calibration'
)
```

The persistent-file exclusion is **subtree-based** and contains only `calibration`. `gate-events.jsonl` lives at the root of `.copilot-tracking/` (not inside an excluded subtree), so `Test-SCDPersistentTrackingFile

title: Empty root `pages/` folder (App Router guide) silently changes `next/navigation` hook signatures to the Pages-Router `| null` compat types
text:
Empty root `pages/` folder (App Router guide) silently changes `next/navigation` hook signatures to the Pages-Router `| null` compat types

### Summary

The [App Router guide](https://feature-sliced.design/docs/guides/tech/with-nextjs) recommends, for the `app`-layer conflict:

> The solution is to move the Next.js `app` folder to the project root and import FSD pages from `src` ... into the Next.js `app` folder.
> You will also need to add a `pages` folder to the project root, otherwise Next.js will try to use `src/pages` as the Pages Router even if you use the App Router, which will break the build.

This works for building, but the empty root `pages/` folder has a **non-obvious side effect**: it changes the **type signatures** of the `next/navigation` hooks across the whole app, even though the project only uses the App Router.

This is not just "a type error in my code" — the **public API signature itself changes**. I think the guide should at least document this trade-off.

### Why it happens

When a project contains both an `app` and a `pages` directory, Next.js switches the `next/navigation` hooks to their Pages-Router compatibility signatures, which add `| null`. This is what the bundled type augmentation in `next` does — `next/navigation-types/compat/navigation.d.ts` (Next.js 16.2.6):

```ts
declare module 'next/navigation' {
  export function useSearchParams(): ReadonlyURLSearchParams | null
  export function usePathname(): string | null
  export function useParams<
    T extends Record<string, string | string[]> = Record<string, string | string[]>,
  >(): T | null
  export function useSelectedLayoutSeg

title: @kozou/api: type-incompatible list filter operators return 500 instead of 400
text:
@kozou/api: type-incompatible list filter operators return 500 instead of 400

## Summary

The `@kozou/api` list endpoint accepts the horizontal filter operators
(`eq`, `neq`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `like`, `ilike`, `in`, `is`) on any
declared column. When an operator is applied to a column whose type is
incompatible with it, PostgreSQL raises an error that the handler maps to a
**500** instead of a **400**.

Examples:

- `?selling_price=ilike.*5*` — `ILIKE` against a `numeric` column.
- `?display_name=is.true` — `IS TRUE` against a `text` column.
- `?selling_price=eq.abc` — a non-numeric value bound to a `numeric` column
  (this value-format case predates the operator work; equality filters already
  surfaced it as a 500).

None of these are injection or ReDoS issues — every value is still a bound
parameter and the column is allowlisted — but a syntactically valid request
returning a 500 is poor DX.

## Scope

Two related sub-problems:

1. **Operator/column-type mismatch** (statically knowable from schema): e.g.
   `like`/`ilike` only make sense on text-like columns; `is.true`/`is.false`
   only on boolean columns.
2. **Value-format mismatch** (only knowable at execution): e.g. a
   non-numeric value for a numeric column, an invalid UUID, etc. This applies
   to equality filters too and predates the operator feature.

## Acceptance

- Validate operator/column-type compatibility (and, where feasible, value
  coercion) before query execution and return `400` with a clear message.

When an admin PATCH/POST changes router rules, this central commit path updates `state.config` but leaves `RouterSelector`'s cached rule indexes intact; `select_channel_with_rule` caches by `router_name:model` and then reuses that index against the new router. If a rule is removed or reordered, requests for a previously cached model can keep matching the old index for up to the 1-hour TTL (or until hot reload happens), routing models through rules that no longer match. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Distinguish dropped pending requests from written ones**

When an in-flight write has pending snapshot B and snapshot C arrives before B starts, this resolves B as `superseded` even though B was definitely never written. For songs, `finishPersistence({ status: 'superseded' })` consequently marks B as provisionally stored and keeps its cover protection indefinitely if C fails or no later snapshot confirms, so rapid library changes during storage failures can accumulate protected cache files that cleanup can never remove. Use a distinct result for requests dropped before execution so only snapshots that may actually have reached storage receive provisional protection.

## Issue Refinement Retrospective

### 曖昧性解決の判断根拠

**[ユーザー確認] 解決アプローチ = 言語非依存マーカー方式**
- 中心的設計判断（マーカー方式 vs. ローカライズ変種網羅 vs. /spec 委譲）は touch するファイルと受入条件テキストの両方を左右する engineering trade-off のため、対話モードでユーザーに確認 → **言語非依存マーカー方式**を選択。
- 根拠: HTML コメントマーカーを grep 検出する方式は既にコードベースで複数稼働（`<!-- phase: -->` @ phase-handoff.md、`<!-- verify-iteration: N -->` @ get-verify-iteration.sh）。見出しの和訳/英訳ゆれに完全非依存で根本解決になる。
- 却下したアプローチ: ローカライズ変種網羅追加（将来の新たな訳ゆれに脆弱な対症療法）／ /spec 委譲（Issue 段階での検証精度が上がらない）。

### Q&A からの主要方針決定

- **スコープを review phase のみに限定（自動解決）**: reconcile-phase-state.sh の他フェーズ（issue/spec/code-patch/code-pr/merge/verify）の成功署名は全てラベル・git state・PR state・英語 gh キーワードで検出しており、ローカライズ脆弱な署名は review の見出しテキストのみ。防御的な全フェーズ汎用化は不要と判断。
- **後方互換 = 既存テキスト署名を fallback として保持（自動解決）**: マーカー未出力（LLM のマーカー欠落）時の防御 + 旧見出しで投稿済みの既存 PR への互換性。

title: feat(retrieval): 新建 corpus 应支持多源检索 union，而不是默认只跑 arXiv 单源
text:
feat(retrieval): 新建 corpus 应支持多源检索 union，而不是默认只跑 arXiv 单源

## 背景

当前 `test_ideas.py --build` 默认通过 MCP `research_ideas()` 新建 corpus。实际新 run `20260606-093116-c0b5ff` 显示：

```json
{
  "topic": "memory based on-policy distillation",
  "source": "arxiv",
  "limit": 50,
  "papers": 13,
  "claims": 39,
  "anomalies": 0,
  "hypotheses": 0
}
```

用户请求 50 篇，但只得到 13 篇。后续 idea generation 只能在很窄、偏斜的 corpus 上工作。

## 问题

新建 corpus 的主检索路径几乎等价于“单源 arXiv + 单条 query”。这对新 topic 或组合 topic 很脆弱：

1. arXiv API 对 exact/hard-AND query 很敏感，稍微组合错就召回不足。
2. arXiv 没有 citation metadata，paper role / impact / representative selection 缺少重要信号。
3. OpenAlex 代码已经支持 `query_variants`，但默认 build/test path 没暴露 source 选择，也没有自动多源 union。
4. Semantic Scholar 目前只用于可选 novelty gate，不用于 corpus retrieval。
5. 检索失败或召回不足会直接污染后续 anomalies/hypotheses/ideas，而不是被 retrieval 层修正。

相关代码位置：

- `src/aigraph/server.py`
  - `SearchService.submit(source="arxiv")` 默认 source 是 arXiv。
  - `run_pipeline()` 对 `source == "openalex"` 和 `source == "arxiv"` 二选一执行。
- `src/aigraph/fetch_arxiv.py`
  - 只从 arXiv Atom API 抓 paper。
- `src/aigraph/fetch_openalex.py`
  - 已有 OpenAlex retrieval，但没有作为默认 multi-source 策略的一部分。
- `scripts/test_ideas.py`
  - 没有暴露 `--source` / `--sources` 参数。

## 期望行为

新建 topic-specific corpus 时，应支持多源检索：

```text
topic
  -> retrieval planner 生成 query variants
  -> arXiv exact/expanded queries
  -> OpenAlex title/abstract/concepts queries
  -> Semantic Scholar search optional
  -> union 去重
  -> hydrate / enrich metadata
  -> local rerank / representative selection
  -> 截断到 max_papers
```

至少应该支持

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve failed email-code attempt decrements**

When a user submits an incorrect email code, `EmailChallengeService.consume_challenge()` decrements `attempts_remaining` and then raises `EmailChallengeInvalid`; because this call is inside the route transaction and the handler re-raises an `HTTPException`, PostgreSQL rolls back that decrement. As a result the per-challenge max-attempts cap never advances for wrong codes on `/email/complete` (leaving only Redis limits, or no cap when Redis is unavailable in self-hosted mode), so the intended 5-attempt lockout is bypassed.

title: Parser.parse and Parser.parseBlock should not throw on parse errors
text:
Parser.parse and Parser.parseBlock should not throw on parse errors

The Luau AST adds an `errors` field when a parse fails, which would be more useful to be exposed to the user, as these errors can then be handled in a way that we want to handle it (ie: showing lints in an editor, or logging the parse error more granularly).

Throwing an error as a string makes this a lot more difficult to handle, since we'd have to use a string pattern to extract the data that would otherwise be easily accessible.

<!-- paulbot-issue-triage -->

## Classification
Bug. Reproducible and narrow enough for the issue-fixer lane.

## Findings
I validated this against the repository contents in `calendar.html`.

- `applyFilters()` skips date-range filtering when `currentView === 'calendar'`, so `filteredEvents` is not limited to the visible month in Calendar view.
- `renderCalendarGrid()` builds a separate `monthEvents` array using `calendarMonth` and `calendarYear`, so the UI grid is month-scoped.
- `navMonth()` only updates `calendarMonth` / `calendarYear` and calls `render()`, which changes the visible month without changing `filteredEvents`.
- `exportIcs()` exports `filteredEvents`, not the visible calendar month event set.

That means the issue report matches the current code path: the on-screen calend

text:
[API] Criar gestão de blocos

## Objetivo

Implementar o módulo de gerenciamento de blocos dentro de um Survey.

Os blocos representam seções independentes do experimento e são responsáveis por organizar perguntas, mídias, instruções e regras de navegação condicional.

Este módulo servirá como base para a construção do fluxo do experimento e para a implementação futura de lógica condicional entre blocos.

---

## Contexto

Conforme definido nos requisitos do produto, um Survey pode ser organizado em múltiplos blocos ou seções independentes.

Cada bloco poderá conter:

* Texto
* Instruções
* Perguntas
* Áudios
* Vídeos
* Imagens
* Condições de acesso

Os blocos deverão possuir uma ordem de execução e poderão ser utilizados posteriormente como destinos de regras condicionais.

---

## Requisitos Funcionais

### RF07 – Organizar Survey por Blocos

O sistema deve permitir que o pesquisador organize o formulário em blocos independentes.

Cada bloco poderá conter:

* Título
* Descrição
* Perguntas
* Mídias
* Regras condicionais

---

## Funcionalidades

### Criar Bloco

Permitir adicionar um novo bloco a um Survey.

Campos:

* title (opcional)
* description (opcional)

Regras:

* Deve ser vinculado a um Survey existente.
* Deve receber automaticamente uma posição na sequência do Survey.
* Apenas o proprietário do Survey pode criar blocos.

---

### Listar Blocos

Permitir listar todos os blocos de um Survey.

Regras:

* Retornar blocos ordenados por `orderIndex`.
* Retornar apenas blocos pertencentes ao Survey

title: feat(autopilot): durable operator-only autopilot pause flag + two-reader enforcement (backend)
text:
feat(autopilot): durable operator-only autopilot pause flag + two-reader enforcement (backend)

## Summary

Add an operator-only, durable **autopilot pause** — a single switch that stops `hydra-autopilot` from both *launching* and *dispatching*, while letting in-flight subagents drain. This is the backend slice (flag + endpoint + both readers + observability). The dashboard control ships separately in the follow-up issue.

**Autopilot pause ≠ emergency-brake.** Pause stops the loop from launching/dispatching new work; the emergency-brake (`hydra:autopilot:emergency-brake`) only blocks auto-merge while the loop keeps running. The two are independent flags and compose.

## Why

"Turn autopilot off" has no durable switch today. Stopping `hydra-autopilot.service` doesn't stick — `hydra-pace-gate.timer` (the sole launcher) relaunches it within ~15 min. The only durable controls are heavier or narrower (`.kill` file = all orchestrator work and is ephemeral; emergency-brake = merge-only). Operators need a clean, durable "pause autopilot" that survives the pace-gate relaunch.

## Design (decided)

- **Semantic:** full pause with **drain** — stop *starting* new work, let already-running subagents finish their atomic unit (open PR / post verdict). Never abort live agents.
- **State:** new Redis flag `hydra:autopilot:paused`, single JSON blob `{ paused: true, since: <epochMs> }` (mirror emergency-brake's blob shape). No `pausedBy` attribution. **No TTL.** Absent/unparseable => not paused (fail-safe to running, same as the brake's corrupt-blob handling).
- **Authority:** **operator

title: Job creation should require client owner id (alejandrorivas-pixel reissue via #743)
text:
Job creation should require client owner id (alejandrorivas-pixel reissue via #743)

Parent bounty: #743

## Bug Description
`POST /api/jobs` cannot produce a job payload that matches the Prisma `Job` model because `createJobSchema` does not accept or require `clientId`.

The Prisma schema defines `Job.clientId` as a required relation field, but the API validator only accepts title, description, budget fields, categoryId, and skills. Because Zod strips unknown keys by default, even a caller-provided `clientId` is removed before `createJob` receives the payload.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Submit a valid job creation payload that includes `clientId`.
2. Parse it through `createJobSchema`.
3. Observe that `clientId` is not present in the parsed result.
4. Submit a job payload without `clientId`.
5. Observe that it still passes validation even though the persisted `Job` model requires a client owner.

## Expected Behavior
Job creation should require a non-empty `clientId` and preserve it in the parsed payload so created jobs can be associated with the posting client.

## Scope
I will keep the fix focused to the job creation schema and focused regression tests.

title: Bug: 睡眠时长统计异常偏高（重复计算 asleepUnspecified 与详细阶段数据）
text:
Bug: 睡眠时长统计异常偏高（重复计算 asleepUnspecified 与详细阶段数据）

## 现象

睡眠数据获取后显示约 14 小时，明显超出实际值。

## 根因分析

`SleepAggregator.aggregateByNight()` 在聚合睡眠数据时存在重复计数：

1. **`asleepUnspecified` 与详细阶段双重计算**：HealthKit 设备（如 Apple Watch）会同时报告 `.asleepUnspecified`（总睡眠区间）和 `.asleepCore` / `.asleepDeep` / `.asleepREM`（分阶段明细）。当前代码把 `asleepUnspecified` 归入 `core`，导致总时长 = 实际浅睡 + 实际深睡 + 实际 REM + 一份完整的 unspecified（≈ 总时长），约 2× 放大。

2. **多源重叠未去重**：`convertSleepSample` 不区分来源（iPhone vs Apple Watch），如果两个设备都上报了同一段睡眠，区间直接叠加。

## 涉及文件

- `VitalStride/Sources/DataSections/SleepSection.swift` — `SleepAggregator.aggregateByNight()`
- `Shared/Services/HealthKitService.swift` — `convertSleepSample()`

## 修复方向

1. 当同一 `nightDate` 内既有详细阶段（core/deep/REM）又有 `asleepUnspecified` 时，优先使用详细阶段，丢弃 `asleepUnspecified`；仅在没有详细阶段数据时才使用 `asleepUnspecified`。
2. 对同一 nightDate 的 sleep samples，按时间区间合并（interval merge）去除重叠部分，避免多源叠加。
3. 单元测试：构造含 unspecified + 详细阶段的 mock 数据，验证 `totalSleep` 不超过合理上限（如 < 16h）。

## 验证

- `SleepAggregator` 单元测试新增重复计数场景
- 真机 / 模拟器上一周视图睡眠时长回到 6-9h 正常区间

title: [observe] Ops actuator verbs: doctor / down / clean + e2e dogfood
text:
[observe] Ops actuator verbs: doctor / down / clean + e2e dogfood

Extends the read-only ops plane with scoped teardown/janitor verbs. Decision logged in `docs/decisions/DECISIONS.md` (2026-06-05: "Ops plane gains scoped actuator verbs").

## Why

Dogfood proof from a live session: an agent diagnosing leaked e2e sidecars (#33) and temp-dir litter (#34) had to fall back to raw `ps`/`pkill`/`rm` — the exact unscoped, untyped surface the product thesis ("CLI at the edge is the agent API") exists to replace. A name-based `pkill -f meshd` kills every mesh on the machine; teardown must be ownership-scoped.

## Scope

**1. Sidecar pidfiles** — sidecar writes `<name>.pid` next to its socket at boot. Closes the one observability gap: an agent evicted from the registry whose socket is hung/undialable is currently invisible (no registry record, no runtime IPC), yet its process is alive. The collector gains pidfiles as a third fact source.

**2. `mesh ops doctor [--json]`** — classify runtime state per process: `healthy | orphan | stale_socket | dead_pidfile` (typed enums per the envelope invariant, not free text). Aggregate verdict; **nonzero exit when dirty** (allocate the next code in the 0/3/4/5 taxonomy) so agents and CI gate cheaply. Mostly plumbing — the collector already computes drift.

**3. `mesh ops down [--mesh DIR]`** — graceful fleet teardown. PID set = pidfiles ∪ registry KV ∪ runtime IPC; SIGTERM → poll → SIGKILL after timeout → verify zero alive → typed JSON report. Kills scoped by ownership (pidfile + argv-matched MESH_DIR), **never by

title: routerctl status で全体 phase を悪化させているリソースを表示したい
text:
routerctl status で全体 phase を悪化させているリソースを表示したい

## 概要

`routerctl status` のトップレベル `phase` が `Error` や `Pending` になっても、現状の出力だけではどの保存済みリソース状態が原因か分かりにくい。

実機 HA 検証中に、controller はすべて `currentError: false` なのにトップレベルだけ `Error` のまま残る状態があり、SQLite の `objects.status.phase` を直接確認して初めて原因を特定できた。

## 実例

- `DHCPv4ServerLeaseSync/lan-dhcpv4-leases` が `Error` / `SyncFailed`
- `NAT44SessionSync/dslite-sessions` が `Error` / `SyncFailed`
- `TailscaleNode/homert03` の stale status が `Error` / `ApplyFailed`
- standby 側で `DHCPv4Server` などが `Pending` / `WhenFalse`

## 期待する挙動

`routerctl status` の JSON/YAML/table 出力に、全体 phase の判断や運用判断に関係するリソース状態を含めたい。

候補:

- `resourcePhaseIssues` のようなフィールドを `status` に追加する
- `apiVersion`, `kind`, `name`, `phase`, `reason`, `message` を出す
- table 出力でも controller 一覧の前に原因リソースを表示する

これにより、DB を直接読むことなく `routerctl status` だけで運用上の次アクションを判断できるようにする。

text:
`pac code add-data-source` removes existing `shared_logicflows` connector entry from `dataSourcesInfo.ts`

# `pac code add-data-source` removes existing `shared_logicflows` connector entry from `dataSourcesInfo.ts`

## Describe the issue

When running `pac code add-data-source --apiId dataverse --table <any_table>` to add a new Dataverse table, the CLI regenerates `dataSourcesInfo.ts` and removes the existing `powerappsflow_llm` connector entry (type `shared_logicflows` / Power Automate flow).

The connector entry in `power.config.json` `connectionReferences` is **not** affected — only `dataSourcesInfo.ts` loses the entry.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a Code App with a Power Automate flow connector (`shared_logicflows`) already configured:
   - `power.config.json` `connectionReferences` contains an entry with `"id": "/providers/Microsoft.PowerApps/apis/shared_logicflows"` and `"dataSources": ["powerappsflow_llm"]`
   - `dataSourcesInfo.ts` contains a `powerappsflow_llm` entry with `"dataSourceType": "Connector"`
2. Run any `add-data-source` command to add a Dataverse table:
   ```bash
   pac code add-data-source --apiId dataverse --table systemuser
   ```
3. Inspect `dataSourcesInfo.ts` — the `powerappsflow_llm` entry has been removed.
4. `power.config.json` `connectionReferences` still contains the `shared_logicflows` entry (unchanged).

This is reproducible on every run. We tested 3 consecutive runs — each time the entry was removed.

## Observed behavior

1. **`powerappsflow_llm` entry removed from `dataSourcesInfo.ts`**: The CLI regenerates the file and omits the connector

title: PR review on VannaDii/revaer
text:
PR review on VannaDii/revaer

Review comment:
The detector parses concrete encoder names from `ffmpeg -encoders`, but persistence only stores codec rows, so the worker reconstructs `encoders` from codec names here. Codec names are not encoder names: `hevc` codec support is not the same as concrete encoders such as `libx265`, `hevc_nvenc`, `hevc_qsv`, or `hevc_vaapi`.

This can make capability validation reject an available encoder, or select an encoder string that the runtime did not actually advertise. Please persist encoders as part of the snapshot run, return them from `latest_capability`, and load them directly instead of deriving them from codec rows.

text:

Review comment:
This path skips `check_plugins_registered`, and the merged segment meta takes its extensions from `merged_index`, a fresh `Index::create` with built-ins only. So sources opened without the plugin silently drop its data here. And even with the plugin registered on the source, the output meta never records the extension, so the new index's first GC deletes the merged file.

Should we guard each source index and carry the source plugins (and their extensions) onto `merged_index`? `merge_indices` inherits both problems through this function.

title: Worktree ref migration: handle packed-refs, not just loose refs
text:
Worktree ref migration: handle packed-refs, not just loose refs

## Summary

The stranded-worktree-ref migration added in #9 only handles **loose** refs. If an older git-zhi binary (or a `git gc` / `git pack-refs` run inside the linked worktree) packed the stranded `refs/zhi/*` entries into a per-worktree `packed-refs` file, the migration walk finds nothing and the chain stays invisible — the same data-loss-looking symptom #9 fixes, in a less common form.

## Where

`internal/storage/migrate.go` — `MigrateLooseRefs` walks loose ref files under the source dir only. It does not parse a sibling `packed-refs`.

## Suggested fix

When migrating, also read the worktree-local `packed-refs` file (if present) and copy any `refs/zhi/*` entries absent from the shared namespace, applying the same skip-existing / hex-SHA-validation rules as the loose path.

## Context

Surfaced in code review of the #9 fix. Loose-only is a defensible first cut; this issue tracks closing the gap so the deferral is not silent.

title: [Security] Refresh token is decoded without signature verification — token forgery attack possible
text:
[Security] Refresh token is decoded without signature verification — token forgery attack possible

## 🔐 Security Vulnerability

### Summary
The `refreshToken` function in `auth.service.ts` decodes 
the refresh token by manually splitting the JWT and 
base64-decoding the payload — without ever verifying 
the signature. This means an attacker can forge any 
refresh token with any userId and role, and the server 
will accept it and issue valid new access tokens.

### Affected File
`src/modules/auth/auth.service.ts` 

### Vulnerable Code
```ts
AuthService.prototype.refreshToken = async function(token: string) {
  var parts = token.split('.');
  if (parts.length !== 3) throw new UnauthorizedError('Invalid token');

  // ❌ Only decodes payload — NEVER verifies signature!
  var payload = JSON.parse(
    Buffer.from(parts[1], 'base64').toString()
  );

  // Issues new tokens based on unverified payload!
  var accessToken = signAccessToken({ 
    sub: payload.sub,   // ← attacker controls this!
    role: payload.role, // ← attacker controls this!
    jti: newTokenId 
  });
```

### How to Exploit

1. Create a fake refresh token with ADMIN role:payload = { sub: "1", role: "ADMIN", tokenId: "fake" }fakeToken = "header." + base64(payload) +".fakesig"
2. POST /api/v1/auth/refresh with fakeToken
3. Server decodes without verifying signature
4. Server issues real ADMIN access token
5. Attacker now has full ADMIN access!

### Impact
- Critical: Attacker can impersonate ANY user including ADMIN
- No valid credentials needed — just forge a token payload
- Entire authentication system compro

Verify — Reclassify the non-last positionals of `mv` (and `ln` without `-s`) as a write/mutation of the source path, not only a read. `mv /etc/passwd /tmp/x` destroys the protected source file, but the table marks `allButLast` as role `read`, so `protectPath(/^\/etc\//, { mode: "write" }).deny(...)` does not fire on a command that removes the protected file. A write-mode protection rule that misses `mv` of the guarded path is a bypass; route the source slot through `write` (or `both`) so a write-only policy still catches the destructive move.

title: P0: Unboks WhatsApp webhook rejected by allowlist mismatch
text:
P0: Unboks WhatsApp webhook rejected by allowlist mismatch

## Finding
Unboks/Marina WhatsApp inbound routing is broken because the ICP Zernio webhook router refuses the connected account before forwarding to `wtyj-unboks`.

## Evidence
ICP logs show:

```text
zernio_webhook_router_connected_account_not_allowlisted tenant=unboks account=6a216ca02b2567671ac6c6d1
zernio_webhook_router_unmapped_account account=6a216ca02b2567671ac6c6d1 event=message.received
POST /internal/api/zernio/webhook-router ... 202 Accepted
```

ICP connection DB contains the Unboks WhatsApp connection:

```text
tenant_id=unboks
status=connected
zernio_account_id=6a216ca02b2567671ac6c6d1
display_phone_number=+599 9 688 1585
```

But `/root/clients/unboks/config/client.json` still has:

```json
{
  "channel_account_allowlist": {
    "mode": "permissive",
    "zernio_accounts": []
  }
}
```

Current router code in `app/routes/connect.py::_tenant_id_for_zernio_account` rejects a connected account unless it appears in a strict `channel_account_allowlist`.

## Impact
Incoming Unboks WhatsApp messages are accepted by ICP with `202 OK`, but are not forwarded to the runtime container. Marina does not answer.

## Recommended fix
1. Repair Unboks tenant runtime config:
   - set `channel_account_allowlist.mode = strict`
   - add `6a216ca02b2567671ac6c6d1`
2. Add a guard in Nr3/connection repair so a tenant cannot remain `connected` while runtime allowlist is empty/mismatched.
3. Add an operator-visible critical badge when `tenant_channel_connections.zernio_account_id` is not

title: PR review on Klvvr1/BrightClean
text:
PR review on Klvvr1/BrightClean

Review comment:
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🔴 Critical_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Critical operator precedence bug in `deliveryFee` parsing.**

The `as` operator has higher precedence than `??` in Dart, so this expression parses as:
```dart
json['deliveryFee'] ?? (json['DeliveryFee'] as num?)
```

If `json['deliveryFee']` exists but contains a non-numeric value (e.g., a string), the `??` operator short-circuits and returns the string without attempting the cast. Then `?.toDouble()` is called on the string, which will throw a `NoSuchMethodError` at runtime.





<details>
<summary>🐛 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-      deliveryFee:
-          (json['deliveryFee'] ?? json['DeliveryFee'] as num?)?.toDouble() ??
-              0.0,
+      deliveryFee:
+          ((json['deliveryFee'] ?? json['DeliveryFee']) as num?)?.

Design: release-stage dimension (beta/preview/latest) distinct from Modifier

## Summary

Evaluate introducing a dedicated **release-stage** dimension on `ModelInfo` — distinct from `Modifier` — to model tokens like `preview`, `beta`, `latest`, `original`, `stable`, `experimental`. During the Epoch‑2 rc2 modifier-taxonomy work these stage tokens were classified as *stage-class modifiers*, but the user flagged that this "doesn't feel quite right — modifiers should refer to altered capabilities or slight modifications," whereas `beta`/`preview` denote a **release stage of a `(family, variant, version)` tuple**, not a capability change. This issue is the design question: should release-stage be its own axis?

Concrete trigger: `grok-3-mini-fast-beta` drops `beta` in v0.2.2 (variant slot occupied by the real tier `mini`) — a sanctioned residual. A release-stage axis would give `beta` a home without overloading `Modifier` or `Variant`.

Target: design now; implementation candidate alongside **v0.2.3** (per user roadmap discussion). No version pinned yet.

## Testing
- [ ] Created tests
- [ ] Updated tests
- [ ] Tested via integration / simulation
- [ ] Tested manually (describe how)
- [x] No tests (reason): design/decision issue. Acceptance of the eventual impl: stage tokens decompose into the stage axis; `Modifier` is reserved for capability/mode (thinking/vision/multimodal/reasoning/turbo/fast/instruct/chat/base); grok-3-mini-fast-beta → stage=beta; cross-provider divergence stays 0.

title: Fix exit/quit builtin dispatch regression
text:
Fix exit/quit builtin dispatch regression

## Goal

Fix a release-blocking regression where `exit` and `quit` sometimes fail in interactive PySH and fail in non-interactive `-c` mode.

## Observed behavior

Interactive:

```text
└─❯ exit
pysh: exit: command not found
└─❯ exit
pysh: exit: command not found
└─❯ exit
pysh: exit: command not found
└─❯ exit
````

Non-interactive:

```bash
uv run pysh -c "exit"
# pysh: internal error
# rc=1

uv run pysh -c "quit"
# pysh: internal error
# rc=1
```

Trailing spaces also fail:

```bash
uv run pysh -c "exit "
uv run pysh -c "quit   "
```

## Required behavior

* `exit` exits immediately with status `0`.
* `quit` exits immediately with status `0`.
* `exit   ` and `quit   ` must work exactly like `exit` and `quit`.
* `pysh -c "exit"` returns `0`.
* `pysh -c "quit"` returns `0`.
* Interactive TTY `exit\n` exits on the first attempt.
* Interactive TTY `quit\n` exits on the first attempt.
* No `pysh: exit: command not found`.
* No `pysh: internal error`.
* Builtin dispatch must trim command words correctly and must not depend on cursor position, prompt rendering, or stale line-reader state.

## Required tests

Add regression tests for:

* `uv run pysh -c "exit"` equivalent CLI path returns `0`;
* `uv run pysh -c "quit"` equivalent CLI path returns `0`;
* `exit`, `exit `, `exit   ` all work;
* `quit`, `quit `, `quit   ` all work;
* PTY interactive session: type `exit\n`, shell exits on first attempt;
* PTY interactive session: type `quit\n`, shell exits on first attempt;
* no output

title: Formalize the ActivationTime/SetActivationTime fork-switch pattern as a shared design

Formalize the ActivationTime/SetActivationTime fork-switch pattern as a shared design

## Context

Two OP-Stack config types now express their hardfork schedule through the same two-method pattern: a single `ActivationTime(fork) *uint64` switch and a paired `SetActivationTime(fork, *uint64)` setter, with `IsForkActive(fork, t)` and every `Is<Fork>` predicate delegating to `ActivationTime`. The fork→field mapping lives in exactly one place per type.

- **`rollup.Config`** — the consensus-layer rollup config:
  - [`ActivationTime`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/f176635fafcd5e7f6dc07b52e391bdc0c249fda6/op-node/rollup/types.go#L581-L614) / [`SetActivationTime`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/f176635fafcd5e7f6dc07b52e391bdc0c249fda6/op-node/rollup/types.go#L616-L649)
