text:
docs: リポジトリと実行マシンの対応（同一リポジトリの2チェックアウト）を明記

## 背景

GitHub 上のリポジトリは `ClaudeCode-StartUpTools-New` 1 つのみだが、Windows 開発機 (`D:\`) と Linux 実行機 (例: 192.168.0.185) の 2 台に clone して運用しているため「Windows 版 / Linux 版が同名で紛らわしい」という混乱が生じていた。

## 方針（2026-06-06 決定）

リポジトリ名のリネーム / 分割は行わない。理由:

- `feat/linux-migration` のゴールは「SSH/SMB 廃止・ローカル一本化」で、分割 (fork) は逆方向
- GitHub 名とローカルディレクトリ名は独立。ローカルフォルダ名を変えると cron 基盤 (`cron-launcher.sh` の goals/hooks 供給元) 等が破断する

[Maintenance] security: Supply chain hardening — SBOM, SLSA attestation, package signing

## Scope

CodeQL (S1) covers SAST on the repo's own source. The deferred work is **supply-chain hardening** — proving that what consumers download from NuGet was actually built from this repo, with no malicious injection at any link:

- Generate an SBOM (CycloneDX or SPDX) at release time and attach to the GitHub Release
- Generate SLSA provenance attestation (level 2 or 3) via `actions/attest-build-provenance`
- Sign the NuGet package with a verifiable certificate (NuGet trusted signers feature, or Sigstore)
- Verify the SBOM + provenance + signature in a downstream consumer to prove the chain works end-to-end

## Acceptance criteria

- `release.yaml` generates SBOM + SLSA attestation; both attached to the GitHub Release.
- NuGet packages are signed; the signature is verifiable via `nuget verify`.
- A documented procedure (in `SECURITY.md`) explains how consumers verify the chain.

title: server: MCP ping timeout を音声系重量クライアント向けに緩和する (SSE keepalive / PING_TIMEOUT_MS 引き上げ)
text:
server: MCP ping timeout を音声系重量クライアント向けに緩和する (SSE keepalive / PING_TIMEOUT_MS 引き上げ)

## 背景

agent-hub server の active ping loop (issue #91) は 30 秒ごとに全セッションに MCP ping を送り、5 秒以内に pong が返らなければ 3 attempts 後にセッションを強制切断する。

```
PING_INTERVAL_MS = 30_000   // 30秒
PING_TIMEOUT_MS  =  5_000   // 5秒 × 3 attempts
PING_MAX_RETRIES = 2
```

## 現象

**voice-gateway** (`kishibashi3/agent-hub-voice`) が agent-hub に接続すると、接続から約 36 秒後に切断される。

```
t=0s   : 接続、SSE GET stream 確立
t=30s  : サーバー ping 送信
t=30-35s: ADK 音声処理が asyncio event loop を占有 → pong が 5s 以内に届かない
t≈36s  : transport.close() → SSE 切断 → WS 切断
```

**原因**: ADK `runner.run_live()` による音声 I/O が asyncio event loop を占有し、MCP `ClientSession` の内部 read loop が 5 秒以内に ping 受信 → pong 送信できない。

## 現在の対処状況

`agent-hub-voice` PR #10 で client 側 resilience（`_hub_manager_loop` による自動再接続）を実装済み。WS は切断されなくなるが、**ping 失敗 → セッション強制切断 → 再接続** という root cause は残存する。

## 提案する解消策

### Option A: SSE keepalive comment 送信 (推奨)
GET stream handler (server.ts line 1631 付近) で 15 秒ごとに SSE comment を送信する:
```
: keepalive\n\n
```
- 中間プロキシへの接続維持も兼ねる
- クライアントが SSE 接続を能動的に維持できるようになる
- ping timeout とは独立した対策

### Option B: PING_TIMEOUT_MS 引き上げ
```javascript
const PING_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000;  // 5s → 10s
```
- 単純変更、リスクが低い
- voice-gateway の event loop 遅延をある程度吸収できる
- zombie 検出が遅くなるトレードオフあり

### Option C: 両方を実施
keepalive で SSE 接続を安定させつつ、PING_TIMEOUT_MS も引き上げて余裕を持たせる。

## 参考

- issue #91: active ping loop 実装の背景
- issue #157: fly.io SSE 切断対応 (`Fly-Timeout-Kill-After: 0`)
- `agent-hub-voice` PR #10: client 側 workaround

SliceRecreatePolicy: `restoredPanCenterMhz <= 0` fallback is unreachable in production

## Summary

Identified by AetherClaude during review of #3316 (merged), confirmed non-blocking by @rfoust. Filing as a small follow-up.

`SliceRecreatePolicy::decide()` has a fallback path for "the radio has not reported a pan center yet" gated on `restoredPanCenterMhz <= 0`. The fallback is dead code in production:

> `PanadapterModel::m_centerMhz` is default-initialized to **14.1**, not 0. So when the pan has been claimed but `applyPanStatus(center=…)` hasn't run yet, `restored->centerMhz()` returns 14.1 — the policy's `> 0` check sees a positive value and skips the fallback entirely.

The two tests covering that branch — `testRestoredPanCenterNotYetKnownFallsBackToLastFreq` and `testRestoredPanCenterUnknownNoSettingsFallsBackToDefault` — feed `restoredPanCenterMhz = 0.0`, a state the production code can't actually reach. The comment in [`SliceRecreatePolicy.h`](https://github.com/aethersdr/AetherSDR/blob/main/src/models/SliceRecreatePolicy.h) ("`<= 0` means the radio has not reported a center yet (pan only just claimed)") and the matching tests overstate the guarantee.

In practice this is harmless — in the #3212 trace the pan center was populated 1.8s before slice-list returned, and even if it weren't, 14.1 MHz is inside 20m which is a common-enough restore target — but it's a real precision gap between the docs/tests and the production state machine.

title: Delta-neutral book monitor (net-delta drift alert)
text:
Delta-neutral book monitor (net-delta drift alert)

## Context
The carry trade (long spot / short perp) and the option structures are meant to be delta-neutral, but delta drifts as price moves (perps stay ~1.0, options' delta changes with spot). We need a tool to track a book's net delta and flag when it drifts past a threshold.

## What to do
Add `btcvol.book` that takes a set of positions (spot qty, perp qty, option legs) from a small config (JSON/CLI) and, against live marks:
- computes each leg's delta (perp ≈ ±1; options via `core.blackscholes.bs_delta` using live chain IV)
- reports net delta (in BTC and USD), per-leg breakdown
- flags when |net delta| exceeds a threshold and suggests the perp hedge to flatten it

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Reads a positions config; pulls live marks/IV
- [ ] Prints per-leg + net delta and a hedge suggestion
- [ ] Alerts when over threshold (exit code or clear flag)
- [ ] Console script + Makefile target + tests for the delta-aggregation logic
- [ ] README updated

## Notes
Pairs with the carry monitor and the structures modeler; reuses the option-chain pull and BS greeks already in `core`.

title: [Roadmap] In-app update — download and self-install
text:
[Roadmap] In-app update — download and self-install

Right now the "Update available" banner just opens the release page
in a browser and you have to download the zip yourself. Better if the
app fetches the new build directly, then either swaps itself out on
quit or restarts and replaces itself.

## Per-platform mechanics

- **macOS**: download the zip, extract to a temp dir, move
  `/Applications/NFO Generator.app` to Trash, drop the new bundle in
  place, relaunch.
- **Windows**: the `.exe` can't be replaced while it's running. Would
  need a small `updater.exe` helper that waits for the main process to
  quit, swaps the files, relaunches the app.

## Common requirements

- Progress bar during download.
- SHA-256 check on the downloaded zip before extracting (otherwise a
  hijacked release ships whatever it wants and we install it blind).
- Eventually a real signature check would be nicer than just a hash.

## UX

- Banner becomes: "Update available — v1.x.y" with an "Install on next
  launch" button (queue) and an "Install now" button (download +
  restart).
- Settings → Updates: status row showing whether an update is queued
  for the next start.

title: Global npm install fails because winston is only in devDependencies
text:
Global npm install fails because winston is only in devDependencies

## Summary

`npm install -g @openhands/agent-canvas@latest` installs a CLI that fails immediately because `bin/agent-canvas.mjs` imports `scripts/dev-with-automation.mjs`, which imports `scripts/logger.mjs`, which imports `winston` and `winston-daily-rotate-file`.

Those two packages are currently listed in `devDependencies`, so they are not present in a normal global install.

## Reported Windows error

```text
Failed to load required scripts. Try reinstalling:
  npm install -g @openhands/agent-canvas@latest

Error: Cannot find package 'winston' imported from C:\Users\...\@openhands\agent-canvas\scripts\logger.mjs
```

## Reproduction

I reproduced the same failure from the published package with:

```bash
npm install -g @openhands/agent-canvas@latest --prefix /tmp/agent-canvas-global
/tmp/agent-canvas-global/bin/agent-canvas --backend-only
```

Output:

```text
Failed to load required scripts. Try reinstalling:
  npm install -g @openhands/agent-canvas@latest

Error: Cannot find package 'winston' imported from /tmp/agent-canvas-global/lib/node_modules/@openhands/agent-canvas/scripts/logger.mjs

This is a packaging issue rather than a Windows-only issue:

title: Resolve BFF-to-Basket service-auth scope gap
text:
Resolve BFF-to-Basket service-auth scope gap

## What to build

Close (or document away) a missing service-auth scope on the path the BFF uses to call Basket.

`docs/implementation-prompts/bff.md` provisions the `bff` Keycloak service client with scopes `catalog.read`, `inventory.read`, `ordering.read`, `invoicing.read` -- but NO Basket scope. The (not-yet-built) BFF calls Basket for `GET /api/v1/basket` and `POST /api/v1/basket/checkout`, and per ADR-0010 every outbound typed-client call attaches the BFF's service token alongside the forwarded user JWT. If Basket requires a scoped service token, those two flows would 401.

Resolve by checking the code (services/Basket -- the FastEndpoints auth on the GetBasket + CheckoutBasket endpoints; the AddServiceAuth / scope config; `docs/adr/0010-service-to-service-auth.md`):

- (a) If Basket's `GET /basket` + `POST /checkout` accept the user JWT alone (no service-token scope) -> document that explicitly (bff.md section 3.5 + the prerequisites) and confirm the bff client needs no Basket scope; OR
- (b) If a scoped service token IS required -> add a Basket scope (e.g. `basket.read` + `basket.write`) to the `bff` service client config + add it to the bff.md prerequisites list, and make the bff.md section 3.5 checkout auth note precise.

Cross-BC auth-contract decision -- surface findings + recommendation before committing if it lands on (b).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decision (a)

title: Instance lifecycle ops aren't atomic
text:
Instance lifecycle ops aren't atomic

delete_instance (crates/services/src/agent/service.rs:2888) calls the external CrabShack Agent API first (:2913-2919, DELETE {manager.url}/instances/{name}) and does its own DB write after (:2937-2939). If the DB write fails, CrabShack has already destroyed the instance while chat-api reports failure — state diverges.

Fix: Make lifecycle ops transactional/idempotent or reconcilable — e.g. write a pending-intent row before the API call and reconcile on failure, or make the sequence safely retryable so the DB and CrabShack can't permanently diverge.

title: Screensaver picker — wire thumbRenderer.destroy() into SPA route teardown
text:
Screensaver picker — wire thumbRenderer.destroy() into SPA route teardown

**Filed 2026-06-05 — Task 8 (code-review) deferred follow-up from #111.**

\`mountScreensaverLanding\` exposes a \`destroy()\` on its handle that calls \`thumbRenderer.destroy()\`. It is not currently invoked because \`main.ts\` doesn't retain the \`ScreensaverPageHandle\` — on SPA route change away from \`/v1/screensaver\` the page is just replaced and the GPU buffers leak until reload.

**Fix:**
1. Retain the \`ScreensaverPageHandle\` in main.ts at the route-mount site.
2. On route-leave, call \`handle.destroy()\` (extend \`ScreensaverPageHandle\` to expose it, threading through to \`landing.destroy()\`).

Low priority — one-time leak per session.

title: [Technical Debt] Severe Lack of Type Safety in Core Logic
text:
[Technical Debt] Severe Lack of Type Safety in Core Logic

## Description
The React frontend handles complex payload structures, including deeply nested AI inference JSON arrays from Gemini/OpenRouter and relational database schemas from Supabase. Despite having generated a `database.types.ts` file, the application architecture relies entirely on plain JavaScript (`.js` and `.jsx`). Because the `authStore`, `api`, and critical views like `TicketDetail` lack type definitions, developers are exposed to silently passing `undefined` objects, resulting in sporadic runtime crashes, misspelled object keys, and unpredictable UI behaviors.

## Impacted Files
- `Frontend/src/store/authStore.js`
- `Frontend/src/services/api.js`
- `Frontend/src/services/aiAssistant.js`
- `Frontend/src/user/pages/TicketDetail.jsx`
- `Frontend/src/admin/pages/AdminTickets.jsx`
- `Frontend/src/user/pages/Dashboard.jsx`

## Expected Behavior
The frontend must adopt an incremental TypeScript migration strategy to guarantee type safety in mission-critical files without breaking the build pipeline for legacy components. All central state management, API services, and heavily data-driven views must be strictly typed using `.ts` and `.tsx` extensions, bound explicitly to the Supabase Database schemas.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Create `tsconfig.json` tailored for a Vite React application.
- Install TypeScript dependencies (`typescript`, `@types/react`, etc.).
- Delete legacy JS configuration files (`jsconfig.json`).
- Rename and type `authStore`, `api`, and `aiAssistant`

title: fix(#921): arvlcd-arrived signal pre-boarding 사용자 대응 (P1.3 follow-up)
text:
fix(#921): arvlcd-arrived signal pre-boarding 사용자 대응 (P1.3 follow-up)

## Context

PR #944 (#921 fusion wire-up) 머지 시 P1.3 follow-up 항목.

## 문제

`evaluateArvlcdArrivedSignal`이 `lockedTrainCode`가 null이면 영구 `undefined`(unavailable) 반환:

```ts
if (arrival === null || lockedTrainCode == null) return undefined;
```

→ pre-boarding 사용자(아직 BoardingLock tap 안 함 = trainCode 미잠금)는 fusion 3 신호 중 1개(arvlcd-arrived)가 영구 unavailable.
→ 다수결(>=2) 합의가 어려워져 fusion benefit 못 받음.
→ 다수 사용자(처음 앱 실행 후 탑승 전)가 해당.

## 해결 방향

- `lockedTrainCode != null`: 기존 동작 (정확한 trainCode match → strong)
- `lockedTrainCode == null`: candidate 역 arrivals에 `arvlCd ∈ {ARRIVED, ENTERING}`인 row가 1개 이상이면 weak signal로 `true` 반환.
  - 다른 신호(motion-stationary, barometer-stop)와 OR 결합 시 효과.
  - false positive 방지: arrivals 없으면 `undefined` 유지.

## Tests

- locked + arrived → true (회귀)
- locked + not arrived → false (회귀)
- locked + row 없음 → undefined (회귀)
- unlocked + any row arrived → true (신규)
- unlocked + no arrived row → false (신규)
- unlocked + arrival=null → undefined (회귀)

## Reference

- PR #944 본문 P1.3
- `src/features/nearest-station/hooks/useFusedStationDetection.ts:evaluateArvlcdArrivedSignal`

## 问题分析

自动化编辑器编辑已有自动化时，“仅保存”会使用窗口加载时缓存的 item.enabled 构造更新 patch。若用户或其它入口在编辑窗口打开期间修改了启停状态，保存配置会把旧 enabled 一并写回，导致外部启用/禁用操作被静默覆盖。

- 调整自动化 update payload 构造：普通编辑保存不再包含 enabled 字段，由服务层保留当前启停状态。
- “保存并启用”仍显式写入 enabled: true，保持按钮语义不变。

**Potential bug: missing `ensureMercatorProjection` call**

Both `maplibre-geoparquet` and `maplibre-duckdb` call `ensureMercatorProjection(app.getMap?.())` at the top of their equivalent `openStandalone*` function (and again on layer load). Raster tile layers typically require a Mercator/web-Mercator projection; in globe or custom-projection views they silently fail or render incorrectly.

The Planetary Computer control serves raster tiles, so the same guard is needed unless the PC library or MapLibre handles projection forcing automatically. If it does, a short comment explaining why the call is intentionally omitted would clarify the design decision for future readers.

title: fix(#921): fusionDebugBuffer decisionKey signal 변화 미포착 (P1.2 follow-up)
text:
fix(#921): fusionDebugBuffer decisionKey signal 변화 미포착 (P1.2 follow-up)

## Context

PR #944 (#921 fusion wire-up) merged with P1.2 deferred (PR 본문 Follow-ups 섹션 참고).

`useFusedNearestStation`의 측정 entry push는 `decisionKey = source|confidence|stationId`로 dedup → 같은 station에서 다른 signal 조합 변화(barometer subsurface flip / motion stationary flip / arvlcd-arrived flip)가 발생해도 entry가 1개로 합쳐져 측정 데이터에서 누락됨.

PR #944로 `detectionSignals` 필드가 entry에 추가되었지만, dedup key가 signal 변화를 반영하지 않아 변화 시점이 잘리고 사후 재구성이 불가능.

## Root cause

`src/features/nearest-station/hooks/useFusedNearestStation.ts`:

\`\`\`ts
const decisionKey = \`${source}|${confidence}|${resultStationId}\`;
\`\`\`

→ source/confidence/stationId만 비교. detectionSignals (motionStationary / barometerSubsurface / barometerStop / arvlcd-arrived 등)가 바뀌어도 같은 key.

## Fix

`decisionKey`에 signal mask 추가. 예: 각 신호의 active 여부를 비트로 합쳐 `${source}|${confidence}|${stationId}|${signalMask}` 형태. signal 조합 변화 시 새 entry 발급, 완전 동일 시 dedup 유지.

## Test plan

- 같은 source/stationId/confidence + 다른 signal 조합 → 별도 entry 보존
- 완전 동일 → dedup 회귀
- 100% coverage, type-check pass

title: Make the canonical original prompt robust: honesty rules, persona input, prompt-injection handling
text:
Make the canonical original prompt robust: honesty rules, persona input, prompt-injection handling

## Problem

`references/original-prompt.md` is the canonical single-file prompt used by non-Claude assistants and by CI for tier-name parity. It has drifted behind `SKILL.md` and has robustness gaps that let a model produce lower-quality or unsafe output:

1. **No "Honesty Rules" section.** `SKILL.md` has an explicit "Honesty Rules (do not negotiate)" block (knowledge-cutoff is real, illustrative-IOC labeling, lab-test detections before prod, structuring ≠ accuracy). The original prompt has **none** of this — its only fabrication guard is R3.
2. **Persona input missing.** `SKILL.md` User Input lists 7 fields including **Persona**; the original prompt lists only 6 and never lets the reader select a persona, even though personas drive the whole output shape.
3. **No adversarial-source / prompt-injection handling.** The prompt instructs the agent to "actively draw on" content from 150+ external sources (vendor blogs, Reddit, pastebins, dark-web excerpts) but never says to treat that content as data, not instructions — a real prompt-injection exposure for any retrieval-backed run.
4. **De-dup / confidence-calibration only live in `spec.yaml` QA**, not in the prompt body, so single-file users never get them.

## Proposed fix

Harden `references/original-prompt.md` (the robustness target) and keep `SKILL.md` in parity:

- Add an **Honesty Rules** section mirroring `SKILL.md` (cutoff, illustrative IOCs, lab-test detections, structuring ≠ accuracy).
- Add **Persona** as User Input #6

text:
Deploy Grafana Tempo

### Description

Deploy Grafana Tempo as the distributed trace storage backend across all three environments. Tempo is the core requirement for end-to-end request visibility — without it, no traces from instrumented services can be stored or queried.

### Requirements

- ArgoCD ApplicationSet (or three Applications) for Tempo following the same pattern as Loki
- `grafana-community/tempo` for dev and test; `grafana-community/tempo-distributed` for prod
- SeaweedFS buckets created per the naming convention above
- Tempo configured to use SeaweedFS S3 gateway as object storage backend
- Resource policy applied (no CPU limits; memory limits on ingesters and store-gateways only)

The cascading-enqueue risk you identified is real: `deployment_events_need_update()` looks at `SourceImage.updated_at` vs events' `updated_at`, and during a live regroup the ungrouped rows keep triggering new enqueues even though work is already in progress.
